title: Renal-normalized urate does not clearly improve cross-survey elevated-CRP prediction beyond separate nonlinear routine measures
abstract: A literature-motivated urate/creatinine representation was added to weighted logistic models containing separate nonlinear urate, creatinine and routine inflammation correlates. Training used 14,403 NHANES III adults; locked transport used 4,596 separately recruited NHANES2017–2018 adults. For concurrent CRP>3mg/L, weighted Brier increased from 0.17026902 to 0.17028050: delta +0.00001148, approximate target-PSU95% interval [-0.00025720,+0.00024592]. AUC changed by +0.00010367. Discovery out-of-fold Brier also worsened. Joint training-refit/target intervals crossed zero; population restrictions and assay perturbations changed point effects. No clear incremental prediction was demonstrated. This tests a representation of already measured chemistry, not novel biological information, clinical utility, causation or equivalence.
